A vigorous [tropical wave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_wave "Tropical wave") moved off the coast of [Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Africa "Africa") on September 22 and moved rapidly across the Atlantic, being monitored by the [National Hurricane Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Hurricane_Center "National Hurricane Center") (NHC) for possible [tropical cyclogenesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_cyclogenesis "Tropical cyclogenesis"). Despite possessing tropical-storm winds as it approached the [Lesser Antilles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lesser_Antilles "Lesser Antilles") on September 27, the wave could not initially be classified as a tropical cyclone, as reconnaissance aircraft could not find a closed center. However, by 12:00 UTC on September 28, the wave developed a closed circulation while located near [Barbados](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados "Barbados"), hence becoming a tropical storm, and was assigned the name _Matthew_. Continuing westward under the influence of a mid-level ridge, the storm steadily intensified to attain hurricane intensity by 18:00 UTC on September 29. The effects of southwesterly wind shear unexpectedly abated late that day, and Matthew began a period of [explosive intensification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rapid_intensification "Rapid intensification"); during a 24-hour period beginning at 00:00 UTC on September 30, the cyclone's maximum winds more than doubled, from 80 to 165 mph (129 to 266 km/h), making Matthew a Category 5 hurricane,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-TCR-1) the first since [Felix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Felix "Hurricane Felix") in 2007;[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-3) the rate of intensification has only been exceeded a few times in the Atlantic since records began. Due to [upwelling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upwelling "Upwelling") of cooler waters, Matthew weakened to a Category 4 hurricane later on October 1, before attaining a secondary peak intensity with winds of 155 mph (249 km/h) late on October 2.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-TCR-1)

Slowly rounding the ridge, Matthew fluctuated in intensity within the Category 4 range from October 1–5. Intensification resumed again late on October 3 and culminated when Matthew made landfall near [Les Anglais](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Les_Anglais "Les Anglais"), [Haiti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haiti "Haiti"), around 11:00 UTC on October 4 with winds of 150 mph (240 km/h) and a pressure of 934 millibars (27.6 inHg), making it the strongest to hit Haiti since [Cleo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Cleo "Hurricane Cleo") in 1964. Continuing northward, the hurricane struck [Maisí](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mais%C3%AD "Maisí") in Cuba early on October 5 as a slightly weaker storm. Cuba's and Haiti's mountainous terrain weakened Matthew to Category 3 status, as it began to accelerate northwestwards through [the Bahamas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bahamas "The Bahamas"). Restrengthening occurred as Matthew's circulation became better organized, with the storm becoming a Category 4 hurricane again while passing [Freeport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freeport,_Bahamas "Freeport, Bahamas"). However, Matthew began to weaken again as an [eyewall replacement cycle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eyewall_replacement_cycle "Eyewall replacement cycle") took place. The storm significantly weakened while closely paralleling the coasts of Florida and Georgia, the western portion of the outer eyewall came ashore in Florida as a Category 3 hurricane, while the inner eyewall remained just offshore. Matthew weakened to a Category 2 hurricane late on October 7 and then to a Category 1 hurricane by 12:00 UTC on October 8.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-TCR-1)

[Video 1](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/1/15/ISS-Downlink-Video_Hurricane-Matthew_Oct-3-2016_428338.ogv?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=index&utm_content=original)

Hurricane Matthew as observed by NASA aboard the [International Space Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Space_Station "International Space Station") on October 3.

Around 15:00 UTC on October 8, the hurricane made [landfall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landfall "Landfall") at [Cape Romain National Wildlife Refuge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Romain_National_Wildlife_Refuge "Cape Romain National Wildlife Refuge"), near [McClellanville, South Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McClellanville,_South_Carolina "McClellanville, South Carolina"), with winds of 85 mph (137 km/h) and a central pressure of 963 mbar (28.4 inHg), which made it the strongest to strike the United States in terms of pressure since [Irene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Irene "Hurricane Irene") in 2011, and the first hurricane to make landfall north of Florida in October since [Hurricane Hazel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Hazel "Hurricane Hazel") in 1954.[[nb 1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-4)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-5)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-TCR-1) Convection became displaced from the center as Matthew pulled away from land due to increasing wind shear, with the NHC declaring the system an [extratropical cyclone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extratropical_cyclone "Extratropical cyclone") about 200 mi (320 km) east of [Cape Hatteras, North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Hatteras,_North_Carolina "Cape Hatteras, North Carolina"), on October 9. The remnants persisted for another day, before they were absorbed by a [cold front](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_front "Cold front").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-TCR-1)

### Records

Matthew set several records during its long and destructive journey. Matthew intensified into a Category 5 hurricane at a [latitude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latitude "Latitude") of 13.4 degrees north, breaking the record set by [Ivan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Ivan "Hurricane Ivan") in 2004, which had reached that intensity at a latitude of 13.7 degrees north.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-TCR-1) Matthew also maintained at least Category 4 status for the longest duration on record for the month of October, according to Phil Klotzbach of [Colorado State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_State_University "Colorado State University"), doing so for roughly 5 days.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-6)

## Preparations

### Windward Islands and South America

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/78/Matthew_WV_20160928_2015_UTC.gif/250px-Matthew_WV_20160928_2015_UTC.gif?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Matthew_WV_20160928_2015_UTC.gif)

Water vapor loop of Matthew passing over the [Windward Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windward_Islands "Windward Islands") and entering the Caribbean Sea on September 28

On September 27, prior to Matthew becoming a tropical cyclone, [LIAT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LIAT "LIAT") began cancelling flights across the [Windward Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windward_Islands "Windward Islands") in anticipation of squally weather.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-7) Schools and businesses were closed for the duration of Matthew's passage on September 27 and 28 on [Grenada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grenada "Grenada"),[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-8) St. Vincent and St. Lucia; schools in Dominica suspended classes until October 3.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-JOSep30-9)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-NNSep29-10)[Hewanorra International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hewanorra_International_Airport "Hewanorra International Airport") and [George F. L. Charles Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_F._L._Charles_Airport "George F. L. Charles Airport") on St. Lucia were closed on September 28.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-NNSep29-10) Six shelters were opened across the island; 133 sought refuge in them.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-SLTSep30-11) Upon the formation of Matthew as a tropical cyclone on September 28, governments across the Windward Islands issued [tropical storm warnings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_storm_warning "Tropical storm warning") in anticipation of [gale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gale "Gale")-force winds.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-12)

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/80/Hurricane_Matthew_October_2%2C_2016%2C_rainfall_forecast_for_Caribbean.jpg/250px-Hurricane_Matthew_October_2%2C_2016%2C_rainfall_forecast_for_Caribbean.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Hurricane_Matthew_October_2,_2016,_rainfall_forecast_for_Caribbean.jpg)

A map of forecast rainfall totals from Hurricane Matthew for the [Greater Antilles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greater_Antilles "Greater Antilles") and [the Bahamas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bahamas "The Bahamas"). Peak accumulations in excess of 30 in (760 mm) were expected along the southern coast of [Haiti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haiti "Haiti")'s [Tiburon Peninsula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiburon_Peninsula "Tiburon Peninsula").

The storm's unusual south track prompted the issuance of [tropical storm watches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_storm_watch "Tropical storm watch") on September 28 for [Aruba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aruba "Aruba"), [Bonaire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bonaire "Bonaire"), [Curaçao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cura%C3%A7ao "Curaçao"), and the northern coast of [Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia "Colombia") from the Colombia–[Venezuela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venezuela "Venezuela") border to [Riohacha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riohacha "Riohacha").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-13)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-14) North Atlantic [hurricanes affecting South America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_South_America_tropical_cyclones "List of South America tropical cyclones") are uncommon. The watch in Colombia was later upgraded to a warning on September 30 as Matthew continued on a west-southwest track near the country.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-15) Residents across the [ABC Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_islands_(Lesser_Antilles) "ABC islands (Lesser Antilles)") were advised to board their homes and stock up on supplies, leading to long lines at supermarkets and gas stations.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-FredAPSep30-16) Curaçao's government postponed the [2016 general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Cura%C3%A7ao_general_election "2016 Curaçao general election") until October 5.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-NOSSep30-17) Government offices in Aruba closed for September 30.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-FredAPSep30-16) A local sporting event, the Kingdom Tournament, was canceled in Aruba.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-NOSSep30-17) Schools across the [Guajira Peninsula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guajira_Peninsula "Guajira Peninsula") of [Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia "Colombia") suspended activities for September 30.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-ETSep30-18) Officials opened shelters and closed beaches across the peninsula.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-EHOct1-19)

### Jamaica

With Matthew posing a significant threat to [Jamaica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamaica "Jamaica"), emergency officials ordered all fishermen on the nation's cays and banks to evacuate to the mainland on September 29. The following day, [Prime Minister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Jamaica "Prime Minister of Jamaica")[Andrew Holness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Holness "Andrew Holness") held an emergency meeting regarding the hurricane and placed the government on high alert.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-20) A [hurricane watch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_watch "Hurricane watch") was issued for the country on September 30,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-PA11-21) and later upgraded to a [warning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_cyclone_warnings_and_watches "Tropical cyclone warnings and watches") on October 1.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-PA15-22) Officials in [Trelawny Parish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trelawny_Parish "Trelawny Parish") placed 60 shelters on stand-by on October 2.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-23) Supermarkets were overwhelmed with residents stocking up on supplies, and many reported empty shelves and low supplies of bread, kerosene, and candles. Many people boarded up their homes and protected their property with sand bags. One hundred female prisoners were relocated from a facility in [St. Catherine Parish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Catherine_Parish "St. Catherine Parish") to another in [Kingston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingston,_Jamaica "Kingston, Jamaica"). Toll fees along [Highway 2000](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Highway_2000_(Jamaica) "Highway 2000 (Jamaica)") were to be waived during the hours before Matthew's arrival. Service at both [Norman Manley International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norman_Manley_International_Airport "Norman Manley International Airport") and [Sangster International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sangster_International_Airport "Sangster International Airport") was scheduled to be suspended during the evening of October 2 or by the morning of October 3.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-24) The [Jamaica Urban Transit Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamaica_Urban_Transit_Company "Jamaica Urban Transit Company") scheduled to suspend services beginning at 6:00 p.m. local time.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-25) The [Jamaica Public Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamaica_Public_Service "Jamaica Public Service") informed residents that the power grid might be shut off during the storm if conditions became severe.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-26) Members of the [Jamaica Defence Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamaica_Defence_Force "Jamaica Defence Force") were deployed nationwide in advance of the hurricane in order to more swiftly deal with its aftermath.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-27)

Schools and government offices suspended operations starting on October 3.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-JOOct3-28)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-29) A total of 900 shelters opened across Jamaica and the Urban Transit Company provided buses to evacuate people from Kingston to the [National Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Arena_(Jamaica) "National Arena (Jamaica)"). Local Minister Desmond McKenzie warned that the infrastructure of Kingston would be unable to handle the magnitude of rainfall expected.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-JOOct3-28) Prime Minister [Andrew Holness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Holness "Andrew Holness") warned residents that Matthew could be more severe than [Hurricane Gilbert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Gilbert "Hurricane Gilbert") which devastated the nation in 1988.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-30)

### Haiti

[Video 2](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/f5/GPM_Captures_Hurricane_Matthew_Before_Haiti_Landfall.webm?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=index&utm_content=original)

The animation shows Hurricane Matthew from September 28 to October 2, and 3-dimensional radar data from GPM's DPR instrument.

Though forecast to pass over Jamaica at the time, the large extent of tropical storm-force winds prompted the issuance of a tropical storm watch for [Haiti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haiti "Haiti")'s [Tiburon Peninsula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiburon_Peninsula "Tiburon Peninsula") toward the border with the [Dominican Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominican_Republic "Dominican Republic").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-PA11-21) Following an eastward shift in Matthew's predicted track, a hurricane watch was issued for much of Haiti on October 1, encompassing areas from [Môle-Saint-Nicolas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C3%B4le-Saint-Nicolas "Môle-Saint-Nicolas") south to the Dominican Republic border;[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-PA14-31) this was upgraded to a warning just hours later.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-PA15-22) The warning eventually encompassed the entire country by the afternoon of October 2.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-PA17-32) Residents on outlying islands of Haiti were evacuated to the mainland.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-BBCOct2-33) Life-threatening rainfall was forecast to affect much of the nation,[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-34) with accumulations averaging 15 to 25 in (38 to 64 cm) along the southern coast with isolated peaks up to 40 in (100 cm).[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-35) Although government officials held meetings on storm preparation, [Radio France Internationale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radio_France_Internationale "Radio France Internationale") reported that Haiti does not have the logistical capability to handle a large-scale disaster. Only 576 shelters, with a collective capacity of 90,000 people, were listed for all of southern Haiti.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-36) According to the [International Organization for Migration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Organization_for_Migration "International Organization for Migration"), 55,107[internally displaced persons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internally_displaced_person "Internally displaced person") remained in camps or hosting sites without adequate protection from the hurricane.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-37)

Provisional President of Haiti [Jocelerme Privert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jocelerme_Privert "Jocelerme Privert") addressed the nation on October 2, urging those living along the coast and in poorly constructed homes to evacuate and comply with authorities.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-HLOct2-38) Despite pleas from officials, many residents refused to leave their homes.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-39) Schools were closed for October 3–4, though government offices remained open.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-HLOct2-38) Nationwide, a total of 1,300 shelters were readied with a total capacity of 390,000 people. More than 18,000 volunteers and members of the Red Cross, community intervention teams, municipal committees, and local emergency services were readied to assist residents.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-40) At least 500 people were evacuated from [Jérémie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J%C3%A9r%C3%A9mie "Jérémie").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-RCNOct3-41) Although civil protection officials took to the streets to warn people, many residents were unaware that Matthew was even approaching the country a day before its expected landfall.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-TWCOct3-42) Evacuations continued through the hurricane's landfall with the total number of people in shelters reaching 9,280 by 2:00 a.m. local time on October 4.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-43)

On October 5, the Electoral Provisional Council postponed the [presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/November_2016_Haitian_presidential_election "November 2016 Haitian presidential election"), the [second round of the legislative elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haitian_parliamentary_election,_2015%E2%80%9316 "Haitian parliamentary election, 2015–16") and the [first round of the Senate elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haitian_Senate_election,_2016%E2%80%9317 "Haitian Senate election, 2016–17") until November 20.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-44)

### Dominican Republic

On the morning of October 2, a tropical storm warning was raised for the southern coast of the Dominican Republic from [Barahona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barahona,_Dominican_Republic "Barahona, Dominican Republic") west to the Haitian border, and a tropical storm watch was issued for the northern coast from [Puerto Plata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puerto_Plata,_Dominican_Republic "Puerto Plata, Dominican Republic") west to the Haitian border.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-PA16a-45) At least 8,500 people were evacuated in southwestern areas of the country by the morning of October 3.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-RCNOct3-41)

### United States

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e8/Richard_Knabb_discussing_Hurricane_Matthew_October_6%2C_2016.jpg/250px-Richard_Knabb_discussing_Hurricane_Matthew_October_6%2C_2016.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Richard_Knabb_discussing_Hurricane_Matthew_October_6,_2016.jpg)

National Hurricane Center Director [Richard Knabb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Knabb "Richard Knabb")_(pictured)_ regularly filmed briefings on the forecast and expected impacts of Hurricane Matthew in the United States.

On October 3, the governors of [Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida "Florida") and [North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Carolina "North Carolina") declared a [state of emergency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_of_emergency "State of emergency").[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-49)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-50) The next day, [South Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Carolina "South Carolina") governor [Nikki Haley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikki_Haley "Nikki Haley") ordered an evacuation for those residents living within one hundred miles (160 km) of the coast.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-51)[Interstate 26 in South Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_26_in_South_Carolina "Interstate 26 in South Carolina") eastbound between the coast and [Columbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia,_South_Carolina "Columbia, South Carolina") was [reversed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contraflow_lane_reversal "Contraflow lane reversal") on Wednesday to facilitate movement away from the [Lowcountry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Carolina_Lowcountry "South Carolina Lowcountry") and [Charleston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charleston,_South_Carolina "Charleston, South Carolina") areas.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-ABC26-52) Evacuations of [Cape Lookout National Seashore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Lookout_National_Seashore "Cape Lookout National Seashore") in North Carolina began this day as well.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-53) By October 4, North Carolina Governor [Pat McCrory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pat_McCrory "Pat McCrory") had ordered that evacuation be mandatory. A state of emergency was also declared for 13 counties in eastern [Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_(U.S._state) "Georgia (U.S. state)").[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-54)

On October 5, [Port Canaveral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_Canaveral "Port Canaveral") was closed by the U.S. Coast Guard, the first closure since 2004. Eight cruise ships and four cargo ships were scheduled to visit the port between October 5–9.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-FT:_Port_closure-55) On Cape Canaveral, home to both civilian and military spaceflight facilities, no rockets or spacecraft were in vulnerable positions; at the time of Matthew's approach, the next launch was scheduled for November 4.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-FT:_Cape_Canaveral_preparations-56) The [Kennedy Space Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Space_Center "Kennedy Space Center") began preparations of the facilities on October 5. Older buildings at the KSC were designed to withstand winds of 105–125 mph (169–201 km/h); buildings constructed after 1992, when Category 5 [Hurricane Andrew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Andrew "Hurricane Andrew") struck the Miami area, are built to withstand 130 mph (210 km/h) winds.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-AT:_KSC_threat-57) At [Cape Canaveral Air Force Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Canaveral_Air_Force_Station "Cape Canaveral Air Force Station"), the U.S. Air Force's [45th Space Wing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/45th_Space_Wing "45th Space Wing") began disconnecting electric power to non-essential facilities on October 4.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-FT:_Cape_Canaveral_preparations-56)

For the fourth time in its 45-year history, the [Walt Disney World Resort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walt_Disney_World_Resort "Walt Disney World Resort") closed. Its [theme parks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theme_park "Theme park"), [Magic Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magic_Kingdom "Magic Kingdom"), [Epcot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epcot "Epcot"), [Disney's Hollywood Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney's_Hollywood_Studios "Disney's Hollywood Studios") and [Disney's Animal Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney's_Animal_Kingdom "Disney's Animal Kingdom"), as well as [water parks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water_park "Water park")[Disney's Blizzard Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney's_Blizzard_Beach "Disney's Blizzard Beach"), [Disney's Typhoon Lagoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney's_Typhoon_Lagoon "Disney's Typhoon Lagoon"), and [Disney Springs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney_Springs "Disney Springs"), were closed at 5:00 p.m. [Eastern Daylight Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Time_Zone "Eastern Time Zone") on October 6, and remained closed on October 7.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-58) This was the first time since 2004 that the parks have closed, all instances due to hurricanes. Other Orlando-area theme parks, including [Universal Orlando](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Orlando "Universal Orlando") resort and [SeaWorld Orlando](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SeaWorld_Orlando "SeaWorld Orlando"), also closed.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-59)

The [Southeastern Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southeastern_Conference "Southeastern Conference") football game between [LSU](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LSU_Tigers_football "LSU Tigers football") and [Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Gators_football "Florida Gators football"), scheduled for October 8 in Gainesville, was cancelled, while the SEC football game between [Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_Bulldogs_football "Georgia Bulldogs football") and [South Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Carolina_Gamecocks_football "South Carolina Gamecocks football"), scheduled for October 8 in Columbia, was moved to October 9. The hurricane washed out [NASCAR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASCAR "NASCAR") racing at [Charlotte Motor Speedway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlotte_Motor_Speedway "Charlotte Motor Speedway") on October 7 and 8, with the [Drive for the Cure 300](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drive_for_the_Cure_300 "Drive for the Cure 300") race in the [Xfinity Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xfinity_Series "Xfinity Series") originally scheduled for October 7 and the [Bank of America 500](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Bank_of_America_500 "2016 Bank of America 500") race in the [Sprint Cup Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sprint_Cup_Series "Sprint Cup Series") originally scheduled for October 8 both postponed until October 9.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-60)[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-61)

On October 6, U.S. President [Barack Obama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama "Barack Obama") declared a federal [state of emergency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_of_emergency "State of emergency") for Florida,[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-62) later extending to include Georgia and South Carolina.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-63) Florida's governor [Rick Scott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Scott "Rick Scott") urged over 1.5 million people to evacuate,[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-64) with Hurricane Matthew expected to make landfall by the evening of that day.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-65) Several [news anchors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/News_presenter "News presenter") also issued dire warnings urging Floridians to evacuate.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-66)

That same day, Georgia governor [Nathan Deal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nathan_Deal "Nathan Deal") ordered a mandatory evacuation for all areas of the state east of [Interstate 95](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_95_in_Georgia "Interstate 95 in Georgia"), and the [Georgia Department of Public Safety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_Department_of_Public_Safety "Georgia Department of Public Safety") reversed the eastbound lanes on a portion of [Interstate 16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_16 "Interstate 16") effective until the following day.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-67)[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-68)

#### Online response

On October 6, the [conservative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservatism_in_the_United_States "Conservatism in the United States")[news aggregator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/News_aggregator "News aggregator")_[Drudge Report](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drudge\_Report "Drudge Report")_—run by [Matt Drudge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Drudge "Matt Drudge")—headlined a five-word comment on Matthew: "Storm Fizzle? Matthew Looks Ragged!" which linked to a _Miami Herald_ article.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-TWP_Drudge-69)[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-Drudge6th-70) Drudge later used Twitter to claim that the National Hurricane Center was lying to the public about the intensity of the storm, stating that measurements from Nassau, Bahamas, did not match the 165 mph (266 km/h) gusts listed in public advisories. The tweets implied that the hurricane was not as dangerous as it seemed and that politicians were trying to "[blame mankind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_warming_conspiracy_theory "Global warming conspiracy theory"),"[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-NPR_Drudge-71) referring to a blog posting about Hillary Clinton.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-NPR_Drudge-71) This came on the heels of radio talk show host [Rush Limbaugh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rush_Limbaugh "Rush Limbaugh")'s claims of the conspiracy to "sell" climate change.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-72) The claims of conspiracy were posted as Matthew posed a dire threat to Florida's east coast and when residents across the state were being urged to evacuate immediately.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-73) Drudge's commentary was quickly met with sharp condemnation and criticism from meteorologists and public officials. Democratic [Representative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives "United States House of Representatives")[Keith Ellison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keith_Ellison "Keith Ellison") called the comments "irresponsible" and urged people to "not listen to this man."[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-NPR_Drudge-71) Jason Samenow of _[The Washington Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Washington\_Post "The Washington Post")_ described it as an "incredible and offensive accusation", and stated that it "may have introduced enough doubt to lead [residents] into a decision they will regret."[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-TWP_Drudge-69)

### Windward Islands

On [St. Vincent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Vincent_(Antilles) "Saint Vincent (Antilles)"), heavy rains caused landslides and flooding across the island. One person was killed in the town of Layou when a boulder broke loose.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-JOSep30-9) In nearby Buccament Bay, a river overtopped its banks, prompting at least 25 people to evacuate to emergency shelters. The Hermitage River rose by at least 3.6 ft (1.1 m) in one hour, and as a precautionary measure, the Central Water and Sewage Authority shut off all water service. Flooding also took place in Vermont, South Rivers, sections of Kingstown, Campden Park, Arnos Vale, and Langley Park. Debris deposited by flooded rivers rendered many roads impassable.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-NNSep29-10)

Strong winds in excess of 60 mph (97 km/h) downed many trees and power lines on [St. Lucia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Lucia "St. Lucia"), leaving roughly 70 percent of the island without power. Landslides and flooding, the result of more than 10 in (250 mm) of rain accompanying the storm, damaged many homes and roads.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-JOSep30-9) Rainfall at Hewanorra International Airport amounted to 13.19 in (335 mm).[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-TWCSep29-82) The nation's banana crop suffered significant damage; 85 percent of farms reported losses. Two homes were destroyed, one in Bisee, and one in Gros Islet; several others were damaged. Roads in Castries, Gros-Islet, Dennery, and Soufriere became impassible from debris or landslides.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-SLTSep30-11) Some damage was also reported on [Dominica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica "Dominica"), temporarily leaving many people without water and electricity.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-JOSep30-9) Heavy rainfall in Grenada disrupted the water supply in multiple communities.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-83)

In [Martinique](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martinique "Martinique") strong winds, which gusted up to 89 mph (143 km/h) in [Saint-Pierre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint-Pierre,_Martinique "Saint-Pierre, Martinique"),[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-TWCSep29-82) wreaked havoc on the power grid; roughly 55,000 people lost electricity. Numerous trees downed by the winds blocked roadways while heavy rains led to flooding. The main road from [Fort-de-France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort-de-France "Fort-de-France") to southern towns was rendered impassable during the storm. Approximately 4,000 people lost their water supply. Three people sustained minor injuries.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-LCISep30-84)

### ABC islands and South America

The effects of Matthew across the [ABC islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_islands_(Leeward_Antilles) "ABC islands (Leeward Antilles)") were relatively limited despite its proximity. Some street flooding occurred on Aruba and Curaçao. Heavy winds were also experienced. There was some damage to cars after street flooding occurred. Outdoor bars and restaurants were damaged.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-FredAPSep30-16) The Guajira Peninsula of Colombia saw its first heavy rain event in three years, leading to widespread flash flooding. One person drowned in a swollen river in [Uribia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uribia,_La_Guajira "Uribia, La Guajira");[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-EHOct1-19)1.29 in (32.8 mm) of rain fell in 30 minutes in the town.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-85) Rainfall in [Cartagena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cartagena,_Colombia "Cartagena, Colombia") reached 8.7 in (222 mm) during a 24-hour span and [Santa Marta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Marta "Santa Marta") saw 5.5 in (140 mm).[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-ECOct3-86) Along coastal areas of the peninsula, large swells damaged buildings, prompting the evacuation of 380 people in [Manaure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manaure,_La_Guajira "Manaure, La Guajira").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-ETSep30-18)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-EHOct1-19) Roughly 70 percent of [Tucurinca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tucurinca?action=edit&redlink=1 "Tucurinca (page does not exist)") flooded when the [Magdalena River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magdalena_River "Magdalena River") overtopped its banks; a nearby bridge collapsed, isolating some communities.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-87) Approximately 73,000 people were affected by the floods.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-ECOct3-86) The dangerous conditions produced by Matthew prevented thousands of people from voting in a [peace agreement referendum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Colombian_peace_agreement_referendum "2016 Colombian peace agreement referendum").[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-LVOct2-88)

### Jamaica

Jamaica suffered relatively minor effects, characteristic of tropical storm conditions. Along the coast, rip currents and [beach erosion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coastal_erosion "Coastal erosion") was reported, with additional flooding due to rainfall occurring. Strong wind gusts tore at the island's vegetation, causing minor damage.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-89)[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-90)

### Haiti

Main article: [Effects of Hurricane Matthew in Haiti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Effects_of_Hurricane_Matthew_in_Haiti "Effects of Hurricane Matthew in Haiti")

Hurricane Matthew approaching Jamaica, Haiti, and Cuba on October 3

[![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1d/Matthew_RBTOP_20161004_0815_UTC.gif/250px-Matthew_RBTOP_20161004_0815_UTC.gif?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Matthew_RBTOP_20161004_0815_UTC.gif)

Matthew making landfall in Haiti

Large swells reached the outlying Haitian island of [Île-à-Vache](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%8Ele-%C3%A0-Vache "Île-à-Vache") on October 2, prompting the evacuation of 89 people.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-91) Despite boating bans, many fishermen continued work in rough conditions. Consequently, two fishermen went missing on the morning of October 3: one near [Saint-Jean-du-Sud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint-Jean-du-Sud "Saint-Jean-du-Sud") and the other near [Aquin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aquin "Aquin"); one was later found dead.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-TWCOct3-42) Antecedent rainfall associated with the outer bands of Matthew triggered flooding in several towns in southern Haiti and the Dominican Republic.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-RCNOct3-41) A person was killed when a tree fell on his home in [Port-Salut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port-Salut "Port-Salut"), while a 26-year-old man drowned while trying to rescue a child from a rushing river.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-92)

Striking the Tiburon Peninsula as a Category 4 hurricane on the morning of October 4, Matthew was the strongest storm to directly impact Haiti since [Hurricane Cleo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Cleo "Hurricane Cleo") in 1964. An anemometer at [Antoine-Simon Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antoine-Simon_Airport "Antoine-Simon Airport") in [Les Cayes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Les_Cayes "Les Cayes"), east of where Matthew made landfall, measured a gust of 107 mph (172 km/h) before the station went offline. Gusts in the nation's capital city of [Port-au-Prince](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port-au-Prince "Port-au-Prince") reached 60 mph (97 km/h).[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-93) Communications with areas in the direct path of Matthew were lost, and tens of thousands of people became isolated as roads and bridges were destroyed. A major bridge connecting parts of [Grand'Anse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand'Anse_(department) "Grand'Anse (department)") to the rest of the country collapsed during a flash flood. 80% of [Jérémie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J%C3%A9r%C3%A9mie "Jérémie"),[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-:0-94) along the north shore of the Tiburon Peninsula, suffered tremendous damage; homes were flattened and medical facilities suffered major damage. A radio host in Port-au-Prince stated that Jérémie was "pretty much wiped out from the seaboard all the way to the cathedral".[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-BBCOct6-95)

Officially, 546 deaths were attributed to the storm in Haiti,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-TCR-1) however local governments believed the death toll to be over 1,000; this value may have been overestimated.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-cedim-96)[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-97)[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-Reuters-Matthew's_death_toll_hits_1,000-98)[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-99)[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-100) According to the nation's Civil Protection Directorate, the death toll was 546 as of October 14, with 128 people missing and 439 injured.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-NG.com-79)[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-WFP_Oct11-80)[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-101) The government initially estimated damages at around 124 billion [gourdes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gourdes "Gourdes") (US$1.9 billion),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-TCR-1)[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-102) but later research found that the actual damages were up to $2.8 billion.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-Govtech-81) Approximately 2.1 million people were affected by the storm, of whom 1.4 million (12 percent of Haiti's population) were left in need of assistance. Furthermore, roughly 175,000 people were left homeless.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-WFP_Oct11-80)

### Dominican Republic

The Dominican Republic reported significant rainfall and [coastal flooding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coastal_flooding "Coastal flooding") due to Matthew. An automated weather station in [Cabo Rojo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabo_Rojo,_Dominican_Republic "Cabo Rojo, Dominican Republic") measured 8.43 in (214 mm) of rain by the afternoon of October 3.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-103) Four people died after a house collapsed on top of them.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-DR_Deaths-77) Damage of the flooding were about [RD$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominican_peso "Dominican peso")20 billion (US$434 million).[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-DR_flood_damage-78)

### Bahamas

Experiencing a direct hit from the eyewall of Matthew, [Grand Bahama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Bahama "Grand Bahama") suffered extensive damage. An estimated 95 percent of homes in Eight Mile Rock and Holmes Rock sustained severe damage. Numerous trees and power lines were toppled by the storm's high winds, rendering roads impassable. Flooding-induced by the backside of the storm affected much of the western half of the island.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-114) Total losses from Matthew in the Bahamas are estimated to be around $580 million.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-BSdamage-74)[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-115)

#### Florida and Georgia

Main article: [Effects of Hurricane Matthew in Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Effects_of_Hurricane_Matthew_in_Florida "Effects of Hurricane Matthew in Florida")

As Hurricane Matthew traveled rapidly towards the southeastern region of the United States, it hit closely to the coasts of Florida, South Carolina, Georgia, and North Carolina. On October 7 in Fernandina Beach, Florida, there was a peak surge of 9.88 ft (3.01 m) above normal. Additionally, in the St. Augustine area, water was reported to be 2.5 ft (0.76 m) above ground.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-126)

As Matthew tracked parallel to the Florida coast, it left over one million people without power across the state of Florida.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-127) In [Jacksonville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacksonville,_Florida "Jacksonville, Florida") it caused major sand dune damage and flooding in the [St. Johns River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Johns_River "St. Johns River"). It also destroyed many properties and knocked out power for nearly 250,000 electrical customers.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-Matthew_hits_First_Coast-128) In [Indialantic, Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indialantic,_Florida "Indialantic, Florida"), firefighters exposed themselves to the storm's winds to put out a fire, which reportedly destroyed a greenhouse.[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-129) In Florida, one woman died due to a heart attack; she had called for aid, but medical services were not able to arrive due to Matthew's high winds. Another two women were killed by falling trees.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-130)[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-131) In the [Flagler Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flagler_Beach "Flagler Beach") area, a portion of [Florida State Road A1A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_State_Road_A1A "Florida State Road A1A") was washed away.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-132) At [Kennedy Space Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Space_Center "Kennedy Space Center"), winds reached 80 mph (130 km/h) at ground level while a gust of 136 mph (219 km/h) was observed atop a 500 ft (150 m) tower. The facility suffered several million dollars' worth of damage, though overall impacts were less than anticipated. The roof of Operations Support Building II broke, and rainwater damaged the interior. Air conditioning was lost throughout [Launch Complex 39](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Space_Center_Launch_Complex_39 "Kennedy Space Center Launch Complex 39") as well.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-133) The planned launches of [GOES-R](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GOES-R "GOES-R"), NOAA's next generation weather satellite, and [CYGNSS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CYGNSS "CYGNSS"), a cluster of smaller satellites which study hurricanes, were delayed due to the suspension of operations during Matthew.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-134)[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-135)[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-136)

Over 250,000 customers were left without power in Georgia after Hurricane Matthew affected the area. Roads were also blocked in the [Brunswick, Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brunswick,_Georgia "Brunswick, Georgia"), area, where all access points to [St. Simons Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Simons,_Georgia "St. Simons, Georgia") were rendered impassable.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-Bynum-137)

### Canada

[![Image 22](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fa/Matthew_from_Hurricane_to_Post-Tropical_2016-10-06_to_11.gif/250px-Matthew_from_Hurricane_to_Post-Tropical_2016-10-06_to_11.gif?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Matthew_from_Hurricane_to_Post-Tropical_2016-10-06_to_11.gif)

Satellite image loop from October 6, when Matthew was a hurricane, to October 11, when it had joined a mid-latitude storm sweeping across eastern Canada.

Matthew's post-tropical remains were absorbed into a frontal zone off the coast of North Carolina. The humidity of the tropical system was drawn into the storm that was formed then. The latter gave heavy rain and strong winds in [Nova Scotia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nova_Scotia "Nova Scotia"), [Prince Edward Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prince_Edward_Island "Prince Edward Island") and [Newfoundland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newfoundland "Newfoundland") from October 10 to 11.

In Nova Scotia, rain amounts were recorded from east to west as 8.85 in (224.8 mm) in [Sydney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney,_Nova_Scotia "Sydney, Nova Scotia") ([Cape Breton Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Breton_Island "Cape Breton Island")), 5.09 in (129.2 mm) in [Port Hawkesbury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_Hawkesbury "Port Hawkesbury"), 4.50 in (114.4 mm) in [Chéticamp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A9ticamp,_Nova_Scotia "Chéticamp, Nova Scotia"), 4.05 in (102.8 mm) in [Halifax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halifax,_Nova_Scotia "Halifax, Nova Scotia"), 3.263 in (82.88 mm) in Kentville, and 1.94 in (49.2 mm) in [Yarmouth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yarmouth,_Nova_Scotia "Yarmouth, Nova Scotia").[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-SRC-NS-154) Heavy rains and strong winds caused flooding and dangerous conditions, particularly in the counties of Pictou, Antigonish, Guysborough and Cape Breton. Several roads were closed to heavy trucks, including [Halifax Harbour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halifax_Port_Authority "Halifax Port Authority") bridges and the [Confederation Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Confederation_Bridge "Confederation Bridge") between New Brunswick and Prince Edward Island.[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-SRC-NS-154)

Newfoundland was even more affected with accumulations generally ranging from 3.9 to 5.9 in (100 to 150 mm) in the central, southern and western areas. Steady rain fell sometimes at a rate of 0.39 to 0.79 in (10 to 20 mm) per hour, and even 1.7 in (42 mm) per hour in [Burgeo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burgeo "Burgeo"). A private station in that community recorded a total of 9.23 in (234.4 mm), while the official station of the [Gander International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gander_International_Airport "Gander International Airport") signaled 6.45 in (163.8 mm).[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-SRC-TN-155)[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-SMC-156)

The rain caused numerous landslides and swollen rivers cut roads. The state of emergency was declared in [Lewisporte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lewisporte "Lewisporte"), [St. Alban's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Alban's,_Newfoundland_and_Labrador "St. Alban's, Newfoundland and Labrador") and [Little Burnt Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little_Burnt_Bay "Little Burnt Bay").[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-CBC-157) The town of St. Alban's, a community of about 1,200, was cut off from the surrounding communities when the main bridge in town was carried by the waters and a nearby community ([Conne River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conne_River "Conne River")) provided a boat to transport people to St. Alban's and out of the community.[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-CBC-157) The highway to Burgeo, on the south coast of Newfoundland, was also flooded and had to be closed.[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-SRC-TN-155)

The winds of over 56 mph (90 km/h) also caused many fallen trees and electric power outages. The official maximum winds were recorded in [Port aux Basques](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_aux_Basques "Port aux Basques") at 80 mph (128 km/h) and informally in Green Island, [Fortune Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortune_Bay "Fortune Bay"), at 81 mph (130 km/h).[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-SRC-TN-155) Insurance loss across [Atlantic Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_Canada "Atlantic Canada") were in excess of [C$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadian_dollar "Canadian dollar")100 million (US$74 million).[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-CBC_News_-_22-11-2016-75)

## Aftermath

### Lesser Antilles

In Martinique, [Électricité de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%89lectricit%C3%A9_de_France "Électricité de France") requested additional crews from [Guadeloupe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guadeloupe "Guadeloupe") and [French Guiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Guiana "French Guiana") to help restore power. Members of the military and Forces françaises aux Antilles were deployed to assist in clearing debris from roadways.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-LCISep30-84) The St. Lucia Red Cross distributed non-food items to 270 people affected by the storm.[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-158)

### Haiti

[![Image 23](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/57/A_CH-53E_Sea_Stallion_helicopter_lands_aboard_USS_Mesa_Verde._%2829564408643%29.jpg/250px-A_CH-53E_Sea_Stallion_helicopter_lands_aboard_USS_Mesa_Verde._%2829564408643%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:A_CH-53E_Sea_Stallion_helicopter_lands_aboard_USS_Mesa_Verde._(29564408643).jpg)

 A CH-53E Sea Stallion helicopter assigned to the 24th [Marine Expeditionary Unit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marine_Expeditionary_Unit "Marine Expeditionary Unit"), lands on the flight deck of the amphibious transport dock ship [USS _Mesa Verde_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Mesa_Verde "USS Mesa Verde"). It is underway in preparation to support humanitarian assistance and disaster relief efforts in Haiti in response to Hurricane Matthew

On October 4, the United States prepared the aircraft carrier, the hospital ship [USNS _Comfort_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USNS_Comfort "USNS Comfort")—which previously aided thousands in the wake of the [2010 Haiti earthquake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Haiti_earthquake "2010 Haiti earthquake")—and the transport dock for relief operations in Haiti. [USS _Mesa Verde_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Mesa_Verde "USS Mesa Verde") and [USS _George Washington_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_George_Washington_(CVN-73) "USS George Washington (CVN-73)") were later relieved by [USS _Iwo Jima_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Iwo_Jima_(LHD-7) "USS Iwo Jima (LHD-7)"), along with the 24th [Marine Expeditionary Unit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marine_Expeditionary_Unit "Marine Expeditionary Unit"). [United States Southern Command](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Southern_Command "United States Southern Command") also deployed 100 troops with 9 helicopters to the Cayman Islands to prepare for relief work.[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-159) Initial estimates indicated at least 350,000 people were in need of assistance.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-BBCOct6-95)

The bridge between the south and Port-au-Prince was destroyed. As a result, aid agencies reported they were having difficulty getting around to the most damaged and storm-affected parts of Haiti.[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-160)

The commander of U.S. forces in the Caribbean reported that troops and 6 helicopters from [Joint Task Force-Bravo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joint_Task_Force_Bravo "Joint Task Force Bravo") had been deployed to Haiti for the aftermath, and were expected to arrive on October 6. These are expected to help with search-and-rescue missions as well as providing medical assistance. In addition to his, a one-star navy admiral will also travel to lead the task force involved in the operations. More than 300 military personnel will most likely travel to Haiti, with 300 Marines on board on the ships sent out for aid from the U.S.[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-weather1-161)

A number of aid agencies deployed to Haiti to help with the aftermath:[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-162)

*   Action Aid reported that over 50,000 people were in immediate need of clean water and shelters.
*   World Nation also sent out helicopters, reporting difficulties and their concern about young children and food. They will be providing water and sanitation for over 50,000 people.
*   The UN's World Food Program arranged for enough food to feed up to 300,000 people for a month. A further 34 tonnes are ready in Miami to be used if needed.
*   UNICEF will be providing life-saving aid for 10,000 people.
*   UN's Food and Agricultural Organisation said it would be helping farmers rebuild their businesses by providing seeds.
*   The US Agency for International Development said it would provide $400,000 for aid to Jamaica and Haiti on October 3.[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-163)
*   Red Cross launched a campaign to raise $9.6 million to provide water, shelter, and food for 50,000 people. They also sent a large number of local volunteers to the south.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-:0-94)[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-164)
*   [Direct Relief](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Direct_Relief "Direct Relief") delivered a large emergency medical aid airlift to Haiti. The organization used a 757 plane, donated by FedEx, that contained 16.7 tons of medicine and medical supplies.[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-165)

### Cuba

The [World Food Programme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Food_Programme "World Food Programme") coordinated with the Government of Cuba to provide food to approximately 180,000 people in need across eastern provinces. The operation would span six months and cost US$4 million.[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-166)

### Dominican Republic

The EU Caribbean Investment Facility and a €50 million loan from the European Investment Bank will finance the reconstruction of housing, but also other essential infrastructure lost including roads, bridges and urban infrastructure. [Climate resilience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate_resilience "Climate resilience") will be improve through infrastructure being built to higher standards and through flood prevention and better use of land. Around 1,000 new houses will be built for between 4,000 and 5,000 people with priority given to more economically vulnerable people.[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-167)[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-168)

### United States

[![Image 24](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a1/Hurricane_Matthew_2016_Fayetteville%2C_North_Carolina%2C_National_Guard_rescue.jpg/250px-Hurricane_Matthew_2016_Fayetteville%2C_North_Carolina%2C_National_Guard_rescue.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Hurricane_Matthew_2016_Fayetteville,_North_Carolina,_National_Guard_rescue.jpg)

[North Carolina National Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Carolina_National_Guard "North Carolina National Guard") assisting with high-water rescues in [Fayetteville, North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fayetteville,_North_Carolina "Fayetteville, North Carolina")

In Georgia, the Governor retracted previous evacuations later, emphasizing that their lives could not be endangered for those who chose not to leave. 1,000 members of the National Guard were deployed for help later.[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-169)

In North Carolina, nearly 900 people had been rescued by boat crews by the morning of October 9.[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-170) In April 2017, North Carolina Governor Roy Cooper requested $929 million in federal funds. The following month, the Trump administration denied more than 99 percent of this request and only provided $6.1 million to the state.[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-171)

### Retirement

See also: [List of retired Atlantic hurricane names](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_retired_Atlantic_hurricane_names "List of retired Atlantic hurricane names")

Because of the extensive damage and loss of life the storm caused in multiple countries along its track, the name _Matthew_ was retired in March 2017 by the [World Meteorological Organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Meteorological_Organization "World Meteorological Organization"), and will never again be used to name an Atlantic tropical cyclone. It was replaced with _Martin_ for the [2022 Atlantic hurricane season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Atlantic_hurricane_season "2022 Atlantic hurricane season").[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-172)[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew_(2016)#cite_note-173)

**Hurricane Floyd** was a powerful and destructive [tropical cyclone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_cyclone "Tropical cyclone") which struck the [Bahamas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bahamas "Bahamas") and the East Coast of the United States. It was the sixth [named storm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_named_tropical_cyclones "List of named tropical cyclones"), fourth [hurricane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane "Hurricane"), and third major hurricane in the [1999 Atlantic hurricane season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_Atlantic_hurricane_season "1999 Atlantic hurricane season"). Floyd triggered the fourth largest evacuation in [US history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_history "US history") (behind [Hurricane Irma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Irma "Hurricane Irma"), [Hurricane Gustav](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Gustav "Hurricane Gustav"), and [Hurricane Rita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Rita "Hurricane Rita")) when 2.6 million coastal residents of five states were ordered from their homes as it approached. The hurricane formed off the coast of Africa and lasted from September 7 to 19, becoming [extratropical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extratropical "Extratropical") after September 17, and peaked in strength as a very strong Category 4 hurricane. It was among the largest [Atlantic hurricanes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_hurricane "Atlantic hurricane") of its strength ever recorded, in terms of gale-force diameter.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Hurricane_Floyd&fullurl=Hurricane_Floyd#cite_note-Legacy-1)

Floyd was once forecast to strike Florida, but turned away. Instead, Floyd struck the Bahamas at peak strength, causing heavy damage. It then moved parallel to the [East Coast of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Coast_of_the_United_States "East Coast of the United States"), causing massive evacuations and costly preparations from Florida through the Mid-Atlantic states. The storm weakened significantly, however, before striking the [Cape Fear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Fear_(region) "Cape Fear (region)") region, [North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Carolina "North Carolina") as a very strong Category 2 hurricane, and caused further damage as it traveled up the [Mid-Atlantic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mid-Atlantic_States "Mid-Atlantic States") region and into [New England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_England "New England").

The hurricane produced torrential rainfall in [Eastern North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_North_Carolina "Eastern North Carolina"), adding more rain to an area already hit by [Hurricane Dennis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dennis_(1999) "Hurricane Dennis (1999)") just weeks earlier. The rains caused widespread flooding over a period of several weeks; nearly every river basin in the eastern part of the state exceeded 500-year flood levels. In total, Floyd was responsible for 85 fatalities and $6.5 billion (1999[USD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USD "USD")) in damage. Due to the destruction, the [World Meteorological Organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Meteorological_Organization "World Meteorological Organization")[retired](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_retired_Atlantic_hurricane_names "List of retired Atlantic hurricane names") the name _Floyd_ and replaced it with _Franklin_.
