Part of the **[2018 Atlantic hurricane season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Atlantic_hurricane_season "2018 Atlantic hurricane season")**

**Hurricane Florence** was a powerful and long-lived [tropical cyclone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_cyclone "Tropical cyclone") that caused catastrophic damage in [the Carolinas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Carolinas "The Carolinas") in September 2018, primarily as a result of freshwater flooding due to torrential rain. The sixth [named storm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Named_storm "Named storm"), third [hurricane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane "Hurricane"), and the first [major hurricane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_hurricane "Major hurricane") of the [2018 Atlantic hurricane season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Atlantic_hurricane_season "2018 Atlantic hurricane season"), Florence originated from a strong [tropical wave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_wave "Tropical wave") that emerged off the west coast of Africa on August 30, 2018. The wave steadily organized, and strengthened into a tropical depression on the next day near [Cape Verde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Verde "Cape Verde"). Progressing along a steady west-northwest trajectory, the system gradually strengthened, acquiring tropical storm strength on September 1. An unexpected bout of [rapid intensification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rapid_intensification "Rapid intensification") ensued on September 4–5, culminating with Florence becoming a [Category 4 major hurricane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Category_4_Atlantic_hurricanes "List of Category 4 Atlantic hurricanes") on the [Saffir–Simpson scale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saffir%E2%80%93Simpson_scale "Saffir–Simpson scale") (SSHWS), with estimated [maximum sustained winds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maximum_sustained_wind "Maximum sustained wind") of 130 mph (215 km/h). Strong [wind shear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wind_shear "Wind shear") then led to rapid weakening, and Florence weakened to tropical storm strength on September 7. Shifting steering currents led to a westward turn into a more suitable environment; as a result, Florence reintensified to hurricane strength on September 9 and major hurricane status by the following day. Florence reached peak intensity on September 11, with 1-minute winds of 150 mph (240 km/h) and a minimum [central pressure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barometric_pressure "Barometric pressure") of 937 mbar (27.7 inHg). An unexpected [eyewall replacement cycle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eyewall_replacement_cycle "Eyewall replacement cycle") and decreasing oceanic heat content caused a steady weakening trend; however, the storm grew in size at the same time. Early on September 14, Florence made [landfall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landfall "Landfall") in the United States just south of [Wrightsville Beach, North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wrightsville_Beach,_North_Carolina "Wrightsville Beach, North Carolina") as a Category 1 hurricane, and weakened further as it slowly moved inland under the influence of weak steering currents. Florence degenerated into a post-tropical cyclone over [West Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Virginia "West Virginia") on September 17 and was absorbed by another [frontal storm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extratropical_cyclone "Extratropical cyclone") two days later.

Early in the storm's history, the system brought [squalls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squall "Squall") to the Cape Verde islands, resulting in minor landslides and flooding; however, overall effects remained negligible. With the threat of a major impact in the [Southeastern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southeastern_United_States "Southeastern United States") and [Mid-Atlantic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mid-Atlantic_states "Mid-Atlantic states") United States becoming evident by September 7, the governors of [North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Carolina "North Carolina"), [South Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Carolina "South Carolina"), [Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia "Virginia"), [Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_(U.S._state) "Georgia (U.S. state)"), and [Maryland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maryland "Maryland"), and the [mayor of Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayor_of_the_District_of_Columbia "Mayor of the District of Columbia") declared a [state of emergency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_of_emergency "State of emergency"). On September 10 and 11, the states of North Carolina, South Carolina, and Virginia issued mandatory evacuation orders for some of their coastal communities, predicting that emergency personnel would be unable to reach people there once the storm arrived. Though Florence made landfall as a greatly weakened Category 1 hurricane, winds associated with the tropical cyclone were strong enough to uproot trees and power lines, causing extensive power outages across the Carolinas. Furthermore, due to the slow motion of the storm, heavy rain fell throughout the Carolinas for several days. Coupled with a powerful [storm surge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Storm_surge "Storm surge"), the rainfall caused widespread flooding along a long stretch of the North Carolina coast, from [New Bern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Bern,_North_Carolina "New Bern, North Carolina") to [Wilmington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilmington,_North_Carolina "Wilmington, North Carolina"). Inland flooding from Florence inundated cities such as [Fayetteville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fayetteville,_North_Carolina "Fayetteville, North Carolina"), [Smithfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smithfield,_North_Carolina "Smithfield, North Carolina"), [Lumberton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lumberton,_North_Carolina "Lumberton, North Carolina"), [Durham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Durham,_North_Carolina "Durham, North Carolina"), and [Chapel Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chapel_Hill,_North_Carolina "Chapel Hill, North Carolina"). Most major roads and highways in the area experienced flooding, with large stretches of [I-40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_40_in_North_Carolina "Interstate 40 in North Carolina"), [I-95](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_95_in_North_Carolina "Interstate 95 in North Carolina"), and [US Route 70](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Route_70_in_North_Carolina "U.S. Route 70 in North Carolina") remaining impassable for days after the storm's passage. Wilmington was cut off entirely from the rest of the mainland by the flooding. The storm also spawned tornadoes in several places along its path, including an EF2 tornado that killed one person in Virginia. Many places received record-breaking rainfall, with Florence setting maximum rainfall records from a tropical cyclone in both of the Carolinas. Overall, the storm caused $24.23 billion in damage, mostly in the Carolinas, and 54 deaths.

On August 28, 2018, the [National Hurricane Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Hurricane_Center "National Hurricane Center") (NHC) began monitoring a [tropical wave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_wave "Tropical wave")—an elongated [trough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trough_(meteorology) "Trough (meteorology)") of [low air pressure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Low-pressure_area "Low-pressure area")—over [Western Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Africa "West Africa") for possible [tropical cyclogenesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_cyclogenesis "Tropical cyclogenesis") within the subsequent five days.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-1) As it progressed westwards under the influence of [easterly trade winds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trade_winds "Trade winds"), favorable environmental conditions, including ample moisture and low [wind shear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wind_shear "Wind shear"),[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-2) enabled further organization of the wave and the development of broad [shower and thunderstorm activity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atmospheric_convection "Atmospheric convection"). Though the tropical wave lacked a well-defined low-level circulation center, the NHC began issuing advisories on the system as _[Potential Tropical Cyclone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Potential\_Tropical\_Cyclone "Potential Tropical Cyclone") Six_ later that day as the system was threatening [Cape Verde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Verde "Cape Verde"). [Easterly trade winds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trade_winds "Trade winds") propelled the disturbance along a west to west-northwest trajectory.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-3) Toward the end of August 31, the system's convective organization became sufficient for the NHC to upgrade the disturbance to Tropical Depression Six south of [Santiago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santiago,_Cape_Verde "Santiago, Cape Verde") in [Cape Verde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Verde "Cape Verde").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-4) While the storm came under the steering influence of a strong [subtropical ridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subtropical_ridge "Subtropical ridge") to the north the following day, moderate wind shear temporarily stunted development and displaced convection to the eastern side of the depression.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-5) Later, however, pronounced [banding features](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rainband "Rainband") developed around the circulation, prompting the NHC to upgrade the depression to Tropical Storm _Florence_ at 09:00 UTC on September 1.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-6)

Development of a small [central dense overcast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_dense_overcast "Central dense overcast") and a mid-level [eye feature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eye_(cyclone) "Eye (cyclone)") signified Florence's intensification to hurricane strength early on September 4, roughly 1,240 miles (2,000 km) west-northwest of Cape Verde.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-8) Shortly thereafter, the system unexpectedly [rapidly intensified](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rapidly_intensified "Rapidly intensified") within a small area of low wind shear in an otherwise adverse upper-level environment;[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-D25-9) the hurricane's core structure, eye, and outer banding improved markedly, catching forecasters off-guard and intensifying beyond model outputs.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-10) On September 5, the tropical cyclone reached an initial peak intensity with 1-minute sustained winds of 130 mph (215 km/h) with a central pressure of 950 millibars (28 inHg), making it as a Category 4 hurricane on the [Saffir–Simpson scale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saffir%E2%80%93Simpson_scale "Saffir–Simpson scale").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-TCR-11) Thereafter, increasing wind shear caused the hurricane to rapidly weaken to tropical storm strength by September 8. A building mid-level ridge halted Florence's northward movement, leading to a westward turn.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-TCR-11)

Environmental conditions became increasingly conducive to reorganization on September 8 as [NOAA Hurricane Hunters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NOAA_Hurricane_Hunters "NOAA Hurricane Hunters") began reconnaissance of the cyclone, with the shear decreasing and warm waters becoming deeper.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-D38-12) Convective banding blossomed around the storm and a formative eye appeared on satellite imagery.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-13) The storm's central dense overcast became more defined, and a complete [eyewall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eye_(cyclone) "Eye (cyclone)") developed within its core. Florence reattained hurricane-status by 12:00 UTC on September 9, with the Hurricane Hunters observing 76 mph (122 km/h) sustained winds at the surface.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-TCR-11)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-14) Fueled by [sea surface temperatures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_surface_temperature "Sea surface temperature") of 29 to 29.5°C (84 to 85°F), Florence rapidly reintensified overnight, and Convective bursts with frequent [lightning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lightning "Lightning") surrounded the eyewall,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-15) giving rise to a well-defined 12 mi (19 km) wide eye. Expanding [outflow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outflow_(meteorology) "Outflow (meteorology)") ventilated the cyclone, enabling continued growth.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-16) The system rapidly re-achieved Category 4 intensity by 16:00 UTC on September 10,[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-17) and Florence reached peak intensity at 18:00 UTC on September 11, with sustained winds of 150 mph (240 km/h) and a minimum central pressure of 937 mbar (hPa; 27.67 inHg).[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-TCR-11) Steady weakening occurred thereafter due to an [eyewall replacement cycle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eyewall_replacement_cycle "Eyewall replacement cycle") and a less favorable environment.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-TCR-11)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-19) At this point, the future track of the hurricane became increasingly uncertain as models predicted a collapse of steering currents.

Steady weakening continued as the hurricane approached North Carolina, and Florence fell below major hurricane status late on September 12. On the following day, steering currents collapsed, which caused Florence to slow down greatly while moving towards the North Carolina coast. At 11:15 UTC (7:15 a.m. EDT) on September 14, Florence made landfall just south of [Wrightsville Beach, North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wrightsville_Beach,_North_Carolina "Wrightsville Beach, North Carolina") as a Category 1 hurricane, with sustained winds of 90 mph (150 km/h) and a central pressure of 956 mbar (28.2 inHg). The hurricane's sluggish movement resulted in widespread, catastrophic rainfall throughout North and South Carolina. After making landfall, the tropical cyclone began to rapidly weaken due to the frictional effects of land, and Florence weakened to a tropical depression on September 16 before transitioning into an [extratropical cyclone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extratropical_cyclone "Extratropical cyclone") the following day. Florence's remnant low dissipated over [Massachusetts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts "Massachusetts") on September 18.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-TCR-11) However, the remnants of Florence subsequently emerged into the Atlantic, before splitting into two separate storms.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-after_Florence-20) The system to the south would eventually become [Subtropical Storm Leslie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Leslie_(2018) "Hurricane Leslie (2018)") several days later.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-after_Florence-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-22)

### Cape Verde and Bermuda

Upon the designation of Potential Tropical Cyclone Six on August 30, the [government of Cape Verde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_Cape_Verde "Government of Cape Verde") issued [tropical storm warnings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_storm_warning "Tropical storm warning") for the islands of [Brava](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brava,_Cape_Verde "Brava, Cape Verde"), [Fogo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fogo,_Cape_Verde "Fogo, Cape Verde"), and [Santiago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santiago,_Cape_Verde "Santiago, Cape Verde").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-23) Domestic airlines cancelled 20 flights on August 31 and September 1; maritime travel was also suspended for this period.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-CV-24) Mariners were advised to remain cautious of large swells around the islands, potentially reaching 9.8 to 16.4 ft (3 to 5 m).[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-25) Under the threat of damaging waves, the Autoridade Nacional de Proteção Civil evacuated 125 people, primarily elderly, from [Furna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Furna_(Brava) "Furna (Brava)") and [Rincão](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rinc%C3%A3o,_Cape_Verde "Rincão, Cape Verde").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-26) Eleven military personnel were deployed to Rincão to assist in evacuations and preparations.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-27) Tropical storm warnings were discontinued on September 1, as the system progressed westward and no longer posed a threat to the archipelago.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-28)

In anticipation of adverse conditions, [Norwegian Cruise Lines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norwegian_Cruise_Lines "Norwegian Cruise Lines") and [Oceania Cruises](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oceania_Cruises "Oceania Cruises") adjusted itineraries for _[Norwegian Escape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norwegian\_Escape "Norwegian Escape")_, _[Norwegian Dawn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norwegian\_Dawn "Norwegian Dawn")_, and _[Sirena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MS\_Sirena "MS Sirena")_ to avoid crossing the hurricane's path and not dock in Bermuda.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-29)

### United States

Video 2[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:President_Trump_Meets_with_the_Secretary_of_DHS_and_the_Administrator_of_FEMA.webm "Play video")[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:President_Trump_Meets_with_the_Secretary_of_DHS_and_the_Administrator_of_FEMA.webm)

President [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump") holding a briefing in the [Oval Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oval_Office "Oval Office") in advance of Hurricane Florence

As [forecast models](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Numerical_weather_model "Numerical weather model") indicated an increasing threat to the Southeastern United States, North Carolina Governor [Roy Cooper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roy_Cooper "Roy Cooper") declared a [state of emergency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_of_emergency "State of emergency") on September 7. Transportation rules for farmers were waived to enable faster harvesting.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-30) President [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump") declared an emergency in North Carolina, granting the state access to federal funds.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-31) An overnight [curfew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curfew "Curfew") was established for [Lumberton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lumberton,_North_Carolina "Lumberton, North Carolina") for the duration of the hurricane.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-Curfew-32) The cost of hurricane preparation in Virginia were at US$10.8 million.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-33)

South Carolina Governor [Henry McMaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_McMaster "Henry McMaster") followed suit on the next day.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-34) The South Carolina Emergency Management Division (SCEMD) and Harvest Hope Food Bank began mobilizing resources for potential recovery efforts.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-35) The SCEMD raised operation conditions to level 3 on September 9, and began preparations for the "possibility of a large-scale disaster", with forecasts showing Florence striking the state as a major hurricane.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-36) Local officials established overnight [curfews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curfew "Curfew") for the cities of [Aynor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aynor,_South_Carolina "Aynor, South Carolina"), [Conway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conway,_South_Carolina "Conway, South Carolina"), [Dillon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dillon,_South_Carolina "Dillon, South Carolina"), [Myrtle Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Myrtle_Beach,_South_Carolina "Myrtle Beach, South Carolina"), and [Surfside Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surfside_Beach,_South_Carolina "Surfside Beach, South Carolina") to limit the number of people on the roads and enable effective emergency responses. The entirety of [Horry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horry_County,_South_Carolina "Horry County, South Carolina") and [Marion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marion_County,_South_Carolina "Marion County, South Carolina") counties also fell under curfews.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-Curfew-32)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-38)

On September 8, Virginia Governor [Ralph Northam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ralph_Northam "Ralph Northam") also declared a state of emergency.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-39) On September 10, [Maryland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maryland "Maryland") Governor [Larry Hogan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry_Hogan "Larry Hogan") declared a state of emergency for the entire state, with the potential of "historic, catastrophic and life-threatening flooding in Maryland".[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-40) On September 11, [Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C.") Mayor [Muriel Bowser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muriel_Bowser "Muriel Bowser") declared a state of emergency for the entire District of Columbia due to the "imminent threats on the people of D.C., including threats to health, safety and welfare" caused by Florence.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-41)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-42) On September 12, Georgia Governor [Nathan Deal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nathan_Deal "Nathan Deal") issued a state of emergency for the entire state.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-43)

Mandatory evacuation orders for residents and tourists on [Hatteras Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hatteras_Island "Hatteras Island") in [Dare County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dare_County,_North_Carolina "Dare County, North Carolina") began on September 10, with orders expanding to the rest of the county the following day.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-44) Evacuations along the rest of the [Outer Banks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outer_Banks "Outer Banks") and in [Brunswick County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brunswick_County,_North_Carolina "Brunswick County, North Carolina") went in effect on September 11.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-45) On September 10, Governor Henry McMaster ordered evacuations for the entire coastline of South Carolina,[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-46) constituting roughly 1 million people.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-47) On September 10, Virginia Governor [Ralph Northam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ralph_Northam "Ralph Northam") ordered mandatory evacuations for low-lying coastal areas in the [Hampton Roads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hampton_Roads "Hampton Roads") and [Eastern Shore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Shore_of_Virginia "Eastern Shore of Virginia") regions effective September 11, constituting 245,000 people.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-wboc-48) The [US Navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Navy "United States Navy") moved 30 ships stationed off the coast of Virginia farther out to sea, to protect the ships and the coastline.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-49)

A mandatory evacuation for visitors and tourists was issued on September 11 for [Holden Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holden_Beach,_North_Carolina "Holden Beach, North Carolina"), [Oak Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oak_Island_(North_Carolina) "Oak Island (North Carolina)"), and [Currituck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Currituck,_North_Carolina "Currituck, North Carolina"). Voluntary evacuations were issued for [Bertie County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bertie_County,_North_Carolina "Bertie County, North Carolina"), Beaufort County, and [Surf City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surf_City,_North_Carolina "Surf City, North Carolina").[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-evacs-50) A voluntary evacuation was also issued for [New Hanover County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Hanover_County "New Hanover County") on September 10, including [Wilmington, NC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilmington,_NC "Wilmington, NC").[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-51)

The [University of North Carolina at Wilmington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_North_Carolina_at_Wilmington "University of North Carolina at Wilmington") issued a mandatory evacuation effective on September 10.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-52) All students were evacuated by noon on September 11. The university collaborated with the [University of North Carolina at Asheville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_North_Carolina_at_Asheville "University of North Carolina at Asheville") to house students who had no options for safe shelter.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-53) College football games scheduled at [North Carolina State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Carolina_State_University "North Carolina State University"),[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-54)[East Carolina University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Carolina_University "East Carolina University"), [Wake Forest University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wake_Forest_University "Wake Forest University"), [Appalachian State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Appalachian_State_University "Appalachian State University"), the [University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_North_Carolina_at_Chapel_Hill "University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill"), and the [University of South Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_South_Carolina "University of South Carolina") were cancelled as a result of the storm.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-55)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-56)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-57) Several universities in North Carolina had announced closings in preparation for the hurricane.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-58)[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-59)[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-60)

In South Carolina, in 26 eastern counties, public schools were closed until further notice beginning on September 10. State offices in these counties were also ordered closed, while county-level officials could decide when to close their offices.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-61)

[Atlanta Motor Speedway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta_Motor_Speedway "Atlanta Motor Speedway"), [Bristol Motor Speedway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bristol_Motor_Speedway "Bristol Motor Speedway"), [Charlotte Motor Speedway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlotte_Motor_Speedway "Charlotte Motor Speedway") and [Talladega Superspeedway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talladega_Superspeedway "Talladega Superspeedway") opened their campgrounds to evacuees of Hurricane Florence free of charge.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-62)[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-63)[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-talladega-64) In [West Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Virginia "West Virginia"), Governor [Jim Justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Justice "Jim Justice") ordered for construction along northbound [Interstate 77](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_77_in_West_Virginia "Interstate 77 in West Virginia") ([West Virginia Turnpike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Virginia_Turnpike "West Virginia Turnpike")) between the Virginia border in [Mercer County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercer_County,_West_Virginia "Mercer County, West Virginia") and [Charleston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charleston,_West_Virginia "Charleston, West Virginia") to be suspended in order to improve traffic flow for evacuees. In addition, [West Virginia state parks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_West_Virginia_state_parks "List of West Virginia state parks") offered reduced rates for rooms, cabins, and campsites until September 18 in order to provide assistance to evacuees.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-65)

## Impact

### Cape Verde and Bermuda

Disruptive rainfall and strong winds affected [Brava](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brava,_Cape_Verde "Brava, Cape Verde"), [Fogo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fogo,_Cape_Verde "Fogo, Cape Verde"), and [Santiago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santiago,_Cape_Verde "Santiago, Cape Verde") in Cape Verde, causing some landslides and localized flooding. Impacts from the storm were otherwise minimal, with no material damage reported.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-CV-24)

Large swells and [rip currents](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rip_current "Rip current") from the storm reached Bermuda on September 7.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-66)

#### North Carolina

Landfall of Hurricane Florence in North Carolina

[![Image 12: Satellite image of the hurricane shortly after landfall](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b6/Florence_2018-09-14_1201Z.jpg/250px-Florence_2018-09-14_1201Z.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Florence_2018-09-14_1201Z.jpg)

Satellite image based on [GOES-16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GOES-16 "GOES-16") data 46 minutes after landfall

[![Image 13: Looping animation of radar data showing the hurricane moving onshore](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8a/Hurricane_Florence_2018_landfall_animation.gif/250px-Hurricane_Florence_2018_landfall_animation.gif?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Hurricane_Florence_2018_landfall_animation.gif)

Animated mosaic of [NEXRAD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NEXRAD "NEXRAD") radar imagery of the hurricane

Prior to landfall, an anemometer on [Cape Lookout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Lookout_(North_Carolina) "Cape Lookout (North Carolina)") recorded a peak 10-minute sustained wind speed of 83 mph (133 km/h) at around 02:00 UTC on September 14. This was the fastest land-based sustained wind speed measured in connection with Florence, but occurred well north the hurricane's eyewall.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-TCR-11):4 Hurricane Florence made landfall near [Wrightsville Beach, North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wrightsville_Beach,_North_Carolina "Wrightsville Beach, North Carolina"), at roughly 11:15 UTC on September 14.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-TCR-11):3 Based on [Doppler velocity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weather_radar#Velocity "Weather radar") data retrieved by [weather radar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weather_radar "Weather radar"), the NHC estimated that the [maximum sustained winds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maximum_sustained_winds "Maximum sustained winds") associated with the storm were around 90 mph (145 km/h), making Florence a high-end Category 1 hurricane at the time of landfall. The strongest winds accompanying the hurricane during landfall occurred within the northern eyewall but were not directly sampled by any weather station.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-TCR-11):4 Farther inland, a peak wind gust of 105 mph (169 km/h) was registered at [Wilmington International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilmington_International_Airport "Wilmington International Airport"), though 2-minute sustained winds topped-out at 66 mph (106 km/h).[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-TCR-11):34 Florence's central air pressure at landfall was around 956 mbar (hPa; 28.23 inHg) based on data from a [National Ocean Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Ocean_Service "National Ocean Service") observing site in Wrightsville Beach and concurrent aircraft reconnaissance data.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-TCR-11):4 The easterly onshore winds produced by Florence pushed a [storm surge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Storm_surge "Storm surge") onto the western shores of [Pamlico Sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamlico_Sound "Pamlico Sound") and the Atlantic-facing coasts of North Carolina. The highest levels of storm surge inundation occurred along the banks of the [Neuse River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuse_River "Neuse River") and its tributaries upstream of Pamlico Sound, where [USGS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USGS "USGS") sensors and post-storm simulations indicated that the water height reached 8–11 ft (2.4–3.4 m) above typically dry ground. Storm surge inundation ranged from 3–8 ft (0.91–2.44 m) along [Onslow Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Onslow_Bay "Onslow Bay") and ranged between 2–4 ft (0.61–1.22 m) along the [Outer Banks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outer_Banks "Outer Banks") and along the southern North Carolina coast west of [Cape Fear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Fear_(headland) "Cape Fear (headland)").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-TCR-11):6–7

The slow movement of Florence leading up to and following landfall contributed to the persistence of [rainbands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rainband "Rainband") over North Carolina between [Wilmington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilmington,_North_Carolina "Wilmington, North Carolina") and [Elizabethtown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabethtown,_North_Carolina "Elizabethtown, North Carolina"). The [training](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Training_(meteorology) "Training (meteorology)") of rainbands over the same areas led to a swath of rainfall accumulations exceeding 30 in (760 mm), and rainfall totals exceeded 10 in (250 mm) over much of southeastern and south-central North Carolina. A maximum rainfall total of 35.93 in (913 mm) was recorded around 7 mi (11 km) northwest of Elizabethtown, setting a new state record for the highest rainfall accumulation resulting from a tropical cyclone.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-TCR-11):7[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-67) The hurricane also produced 27 tornadoes in North Carolina.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-TCR-11):8 Damage statewide reached an estimated US$17 billion, more than the combined damage of Hurricane Floyd and [Hurricane Matthew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew "Hurricane Matthew") in the state, according to Governor Roy Cooper.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-historic-68) Estimated insurance losses ranged between $2.8–5 billion.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-Insurance_loss-69) Hurricane-related flooding damaged an estimated seventy-five thousand structures, many of which had been previously damaged in Hurricane Matthew.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-FlorenceObserver2020-70)

In [Wrightsville Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wrightsville_Beach,_North_Carolina "Wrightsville Beach, North Carolina"), North Carolina, 27 people required lifeguard rescue between September 8 and 9.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-71) On September 13, [New Bern, North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Bern,_North_Carolina "New Bern, North Carolina"), was inundated with storm surge around 6 feet (1.8 m). Water levels rose in the west side of the [Pamlico Sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamlico_Sound "Pamlico Sound"). Water levels on the Neuse River at [Oriental, North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oriental,_North_Carolina "Oriental, North Carolina") peaked at 9.6 feet above normal.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-72) Employees at [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company "American Broadcasting Company") affiliate [WCTI-TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WCTI-TV "WCTI-TV") (which serves the surrounding market that includes [Greenville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greenville,_North_Carolina "Greenville, North Carolina") and [Jacksonville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacksonville,_North_Carolina "Jacksonville, North Carolina")) were forced to evacuate its New Bern studio facility that evening due to the rising waters, with WCTI switching to a simulcast of [Sinclair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinclair_Broadcast_Group "Sinclair Broadcast Group") sister station [WPDE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WPDE "WPDE")'s live coverage of the storm until station staff could resume their own broadcasts.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-73)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-74)[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-75) Reports indicated that around 150 people were in need of rescue in New Bern because of the heavy flooding.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-76)

Florence's flooding in North Carolina and Virginia was compounded by earlier flooding during the summer that left the ground heavily saturated.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-77)

Florence made landfall in [Wrightsville Beach, North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wrightsville_Beach,_North_Carolina "Wrightsville Beach, North Carolina") on September 14, and by mid-morning rescuers had already evacuated more than 200 people from floodwaters, with about 150 more awaiting rescue. The storm had reportedly cut power to more than 500,000 customers in North and South Carolina by the time of landfall and caused the roof of a hotel in [Jacksonville, North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacksonville,_North_Carolina "Jacksonville, North Carolina") to collapse that morning.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-78) On September 14, about 100 civilians, city workers, and [National Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Guard_of_the_United_States "National Guard of the United States") worked to fill sandbags and protect [Lumberton, North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lumberton,_North_Carolina "Lumberton, North Carolina") from an identified weak spot that caused massive flooding during [Hurricane Matthew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew "Hurricane Matthew") in 2016.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-79)

Heavy rains continued to affect the Carolinas after landfall. A [weather station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weather_station "Weather station") in [Swansboro, North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swansboro,_North_Carolina "Swansboro, North Carolina"), recorded 33.90 inches (861 mm) of [rain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rain "Rain"), establishing a new record for a tropical cyclone in that state.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-preliminary_totals_for_Florence-80)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-TCR-11)[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-NCrain-81)[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-SCrain-82) By September 17, Florence had dropped a maximum total of 35.93 inches (913 mm) of rain in [Elizabethtown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabethtown,_North_Carolina "Elizabethtown, North Carolina"), North Carolina, becoming the wettest tropical cyclone recorded in the state.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-preliminary_totals_for_Florence-80)

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9d/Hurricane_Florence_rainfall.png/250px-Hurricane_Florence_rainfall.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Hurricane_Florence_rainfall.png)

5-day map accumulation with Florence over the Carolinas

Statewide, approximately 2,200 primary and secondary roads closed due to flooding,[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-NPR_0920-83) including large sections of Interstates [40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_40 "Interstate 40") and [95](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_95 "Interstate 95").[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-84)[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-85)

Strong winds in [New Hanover County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Hanover_County,_North_Carolina "New Hanover County, North Carolina") toppled numerous trees and power lines, while more than 90% of the county was left without electricity. The storm dropped up to 27.2 in (690 mm) of rain near [Kings Grant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kings_Grant,_North_Carolina "Kings Grant, North Carolina").[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-nwsilm-86) By the morning of September 16, Wilmington had recorded more rain from Florence than any other single weather event in the city's history. Additionally, Florence contributed to the wettest year in Wilmington history, with annual rainfall totals eclipsing the previous record set in 1877.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-KILM-PNS-161405-87) The city of Wilmington became entirely isolated, as all roads to the city flooded and were deemed impassable,[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-WP_0916-88) and the city's airport and seaport were also closed.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-WP_0916-88)[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-89) Although cell phone service remained operational, excess demand strained networks. More than 450 people required rescue across Wilmington. Woody White, New Hanover County chairman of the board of commissioners, issued a statement advising all travelers to avoid the Wilmington area.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-WP_0916-88) There was a report of looting and burglary at a Wilmington area [Family Dollar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Family_Dollar "Family Dollar"), with the theft of non-essential items such as [sports apparel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sportswear_(activewear) "Sportswear (activewear)") and [athletic shoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletic_shoes "Athletic shoes") during the height of the storm.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-90)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-91) The city-wide curfew issued in advance of the storm was extended because of these incidents.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-WP_0916-88)

Early on September 17, a tornado was confirmed in [Elm City, North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elm_City,_North_Carolina "Elm City, North Carolina").[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-92)

Also on September 17, the [Pee Dee River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pee_Dee_River "Pee Dee River") crested at [Ansonville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ansonville,_North_Carolina "Ansonville, North Carolina") at 35.4 ft (10.8 m), 2 ft (0.61 m) above the 1945 record.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-93)

The [Cape Fear River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Fear_River "Cape Fear River") crested at 61.4 ft (18.7 m)—about 35 ft (11 m) above flood stage—near [Fayetteville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fayetteville,_North_Carolina "Fayetteville, North Carolina") early on September 19. The magnitude of flooding greatly exceeded the levels observed due to [Hurricane Matthew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Matthew "Hurricane Matthew") in 2016. The nearby Little River inundated large areas across [Cumberland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cumberland_County,_North_Carolina "Cumberland County, North Carolina") and [Harnett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harnett_County,_North_Carolina "Harnett County, North Carolina") counties. Overtopped bridges isolated communities and hampered relief efforts.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-94)

#### South Carolina

[![Image 15](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c3/Florence_2018-09-15_1820Z.jpg/250px-Florence_2018-09-15_1820Z.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Florence_2018-09-15_1820Z.jpg)

Hurricane Florence about a day after landfall over the Carolinas, on September 15

Heavy rainfall also occurred in South Carolina, with 23.63 in (600 mm) of precipitation observed near [Loris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loris,_South_Carolina "Loris, South Carolina"), setting a new state record for rainfall from a tropical cyclone.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-SCrainsWPC-95) More than 100 people were rescued from their homes and cars in Loris. The [Waccamaw River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waccamaw_River "Waccamaw River") in [Conway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conway,_South_Carolina "Conway, South Carolina") crested at 22.1 ft (6.7 m) on September 26, exceeding the Hurricane Matthew record of 19.1 ft (5.8 m). At a neighborhood along [South Carolina Highway 905](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Carolina_Highway_905 "South Carolina Highway 905"), about 5 ft (1.5 m) of water entered some homes. Farther south along the Waccamaw River, homes in a neighborhood in [Socastee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Socastee,_South_Carolina "Socastee, South Carolina") were flooded with as much as 8 ft (2.4 m) of water. In western [Horry County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horry_County,_South_Carolina "Horry County, South Carolina"), the community of Dongola was left isolated for 10 days. The overflowing river flooded almost 1,000 homes and businesses. The storm also spawned two tornadoes in Horry County, both rated EF0. The first tornado touched down just north-northeast of [Myrtle Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Myrtle_Beach,_South_Carolina "Myrtle Beach, South Carolina"), causing minor damage to pine trees near [Route 17](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Route_17 "U.S. Route 17") before lifting after moving only about half a mile. The other tornado touched down near [Longs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Longs,_South_Carolina "Longs, South Carolina") and also damaged pine trees and a roof.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-nwsilm-86)

Flooding was also reported in [Marion County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marion_County,_South_Carolina "Marion County, South Carolina"), especially in [Brittons Neck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brittons_Neck,_South_Carolina "Brittons Neck, South Carolina") and [Gresham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gresham,_South_Carolina "Gresham, South Carolina"). A number of people evacuated and were still not able to access their homes by October 1. In [Nichols](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nichols,_South_Carolina "Nichols, South Carolina"), flooding damaged about 150 homes which had been rebuilt after Hurricane Matthew. Strong winds downed trees and power lines, while at least one home in Nichols suffered roof damage. Approximately 400 homes in [Dillon County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dillon_County,_South_Carolina "Dillon County, South Carolina") were flooded. A total of 21 homes in [Darlington County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darlington_County,_South_Carolina "Darlington County, South Carolina") received severe flood damage, while another home was destroyed.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-nwsilm-86)

In [Chesterfield County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chesterfield_County,_South_Carolina "Chesterfield County, South Carolina"), the [Pee Dee River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pee_Dee_River "Pee Dee River") crested at 46.51 ft (14.18 m) at [Cheraw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheraw,_South_Carolina "Cheraw, South Carolina"). Three nearby dams failed, causing significant flooding in Cheraw and the town of [Chesterfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chesterfield,_South_Carolina "Chesterfield, South Carolina"). Many roads became impassable or were washed out. A total of 226 homes were damaged and other 2 were destroyed.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-nwscae-96) A [Superfund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superfund "Superfund") site was also damaged, causing [PCB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polychlorinated_biphenyl "Polychlorinated biphenyl") to enter homes, a toxic substance which required cleanup efforts by the [Environmental Protection Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Environmental_Protection_Agency "United States Environmental Protection Agency").[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-97) In [Lancaster County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lancaster_County,_South_Carolina "Lancaster County, South Carolina"), flash flooding left a number of roads impassable and washed out several other streets. A park was flooded after the [Gills Creek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gills_Creek "Gills Creek") overflowed. Winds downed about 20 trees in the [Lancaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lancaster,_South_Carolina "Lancaster, South Carolina") area, one of which fell onto a home and others falling onto a road. Power lines were downed across [Route 521](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Route_521 "U.S. Route 521"), obstructing all four lanes.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-nwscae-96) Damage statewide were at least $1.2 billion.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-98)

#### Elsewhere

[![Image 16](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0f/Olddominionflorence.jpg/250px-Olddominionflorence.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Olddominionflorence.jpg)

A warehouse in Chesterfield County, Virginia, destroyed by a tornado

The storm spawned 10 tornadoes in Virginia, including 2 in [Chesterfield County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chesterfield_County,_Virginia "Chesterfield County, Virginia"), 1 in [Hanover County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hanover_County,_Virginia "Hanover County, Virginia"), 1 in [Mecklenburg County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mecklenburg_County,_Virginia "Mecklenburg County, Virginia"), 1 in [Powhatan County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Powhatan_County,_Virginia "Powhatan County, Virginia"), and 5 in [Richmond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richmond,_Virginia "Richmond, Virginia"). Most of these tornadoes caused little damage other than downed trees, tree limbs, or electrical poles. However, the twister in Chesterfield County, rated EF2, damaged several buildings between [Winterpock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winterpock,_Virginia "Winterpock, Virginia") and [Bon Air](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Air,_Virginia "Bon Air, Virginia") and destroyed a warehouse, causing one death and at least one injury. The tornado in Mecklenburg County, rated EF0, touched down between [Boydton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boydton,_Virginia "Boydton, Virginia") and [Skipwith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skipwith,_Virginia "Skipwith, Virginia"). Extensive tree damage was reported, with several homes and outbuildings damaged by falling trees.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-nwsakqtornado-99) Additionally, [Shenandoah National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shenandoah_National_Park "Shenandoah National Park") was closed due to severe weather.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-100) Virginia suffered a total of $200 million in damages.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-TCR-11)

The state of [Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_(U.S._state) "Georgia (U.S. state)") experienced lesser amounts of damage, mostly from fallen trees and downed powerlines. Damage in Georgia totaled $30 million.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-TCR-11)

Large [swells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swell_(ocean) "Swell (ocean)") ahead of the hurricane reached [Assateague State Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assateague_State_Park "Assateague State Park"), Maryland, by September 9, prompting the [Maryland Department of Natural Resources](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maryland_Department_of_Natural_Resources "Maryland Department of Natural Resources") to close beach access indefinitely.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-101)

Over 4 in (100 mm) of rain fell in portions of [Upstate New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upstate_New_York "Upstate New York"), prompting numerous flood warnings, and closing several roads.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-102) In some areas, rainfall rates exceeded 1 in (25 mm) per hour.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-103) Farther south, the remnants of Florence produced record rainfall at [LaGuardia Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LaGuardia_Airport "LaGuardia Airport") on September 18,[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-104) and the [New York City Subway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City_Subway "New York City Subway") system flooded as well.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-105) Flash flood damage in New York caused $473,000 in damage.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-106)

Two people in [North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Carolina "North Carolina") died while trying to evacuate: one in [Columbus County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbus_County,_North_Carolina "Columbus County, North Carolina") and [Wayne County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wayne_County,_North_Carolina "Wayne County, North Carolina").[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-CT_0916-110)[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-CO_0917-111) In [Wilmington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilmington,_North_Carolina "Wilmington, North Carolina"), a mother and her baby were killed when a tree landed on their house. In [Hampstead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hampstead,_North_Carolina "Hampstead, North Carolina"), a woman died of a heart attack; downed trees on roads kept first responders from reaching her. A person was [electrocuted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electrocution "Electrocution") in [Lenoir County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lenoir_County,_North_Carolina "Lenoir County, North Carolina") while plugging in a generator in the wet conditions.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-112) A house fire in [Fayetteville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fayetteville,_North_Carolina "Fayetteville, North Carolina") killed a husband and wife. Freshwater flooding killed at least eleven people: one in [Anson County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anson_County,_North_Carolina "Anson County, North Carolina"), eight [Duplin County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duplin_County,_North_Carolina "Duplin County, North Carolina"), and two in [Scotland County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scotland_County,_North_Carolina "Scotland County, North Carolina").[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-NPR_0920-83)[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-CO_0917-111)[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-WTOP_0916-113) One man was killed in [Kinston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinston,_North_Carolina "Kinston, North Carolina") by strong winds while checking on his hunting dogs.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-114) A three-month-old baby died in [Gaston County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaston_County,_North_Carolina "Gaston County, North Carolina") when a tree crushed a mobile home.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-CT_0916-110) In [Union County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Union_County,_North_Carolina "Union County, North Carolina"), a woman drove around a barrier into a flooded road and her vehicle was swept away. Rescuers saved the mother, but her one-year-old baby drowned.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-115) An [18-wheeler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/18-wheeler "18-wheeler")[aquaplaned](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aquaplaning "Aquaplaning") off [Interstate 85](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_85 "Interstate 85") near [Kings Mountain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kings_Mountain,_North_Carolina "Kings Mountain, North Carolina") and crashed into a tree; the vehicle tore in half, killing the driver.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-116) Two other accidents each killed one person: an elderly man died of oxygen loss related to [chronic obstructive pulmonary disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chronic_obstructive_pulmonary_disease "Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease") during a power outage, and a person collapsed and died in [Sampson County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sampson_County,_North_Carolina "Sampson County, North Carolina") while helping an evacuee.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-CO_0917-111) One person drowned in the swelling [Cape Fear River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Fear_River "Cape Fear River") near Cedar Creek after refusing evacuation orders.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-117) On September 20, a man in [Brunswick County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brunswick_County,_North_Carolina "Brunswick County, North Carolina") died after being crushed by a tree he was clearing.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-118) In late September, two people were killed in North Carolina while repairing damage from Hurricane Florence to their homes, bringing the death toll in the state to 39.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-death_toll_rises-119)

Three deaths originally attributed to the hurricane were later considered unrelated. One woman died of unknown causes in a shelter, and two people found dead on [Harkers Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harkers_Island,_North_Carolina "Harkers Island, North Carolina") were deemed victims of a [murder-suicide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murder-suicide "Murder-suicide").[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-CT_0916-110)[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-120)

Two people died of [carbon monoxide poisoning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carbon_monoxide_poisoning "Carbon monoxide poisoning") in [Loris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loris,_South_Carolina "Loris, South Carolina"), South Carolina. A vehicle with three occupants lost control on a flooded road in [Georgetown County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgetown_County,_South_Carolina "Georgetown County, South Carolina"); one passenger died, while the driver and other passenger escaped. A woman died when her vehicle crashed into a downed tree near [Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Union,_South_Carolina "Union, South Carolina").[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-WTOP_0916-113) A vehicle lost control along [Interstate 20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_20 "Interstate 20") near [Columbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia,_South_Carolina "Columbia, South Carolina") and crashed into a bridge support, killing the driver. Another fatal accident occurred near Columbia when a woman drove into a flooded road and crashed into a tree.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-121) On September 18, a van was transporting two mental health patients from [Horry County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horry_County,_South_Carolina "Horry County, South Carolina") to [Darlington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darlington,_South_Carolina "Darlington, South Carolina"); the vehicle was swept away by swift-moving water along [U.S. Route 76](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Route_76 "U.S. Route 76")—the swollen [Little Pee Dee River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little_Pee_Dee_River "Little Pee Dee River") was 0.5 mi (0.80 km) from this location.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-122) The two deputies in the van managed to escape and survived;[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-123) however, the two women in the back were shackled and drowned.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-124) The deputies were put on [administrative leave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Administrative_leave "Administrative leave").[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-:0-125)

On September 17, ten tornadoes of strengths between EF0 and EF2 [[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-nwsakqtornado-99)[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-126) touched down in Virginia, resulting in one death in [Chesterfield County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chesterfield_County,_Virginia "Chesterfield County, Virginia"), [Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia "Virginia").[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-127)[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-128) Another person died when his vehicle was swept away along a flooded road in [Louisa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisa,_Virginia "Louisa, Virginia").[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-129)

A 69-year-old man in [Robeson County, North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robeson_County,_North_Carolina "Robeson County, North Carolina") whose house was damaged apparently committed suicide.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-month-130)[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-131)

#### Agriculture and environmental effects

[![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/21/20180924-OSEC-LSC-1160_%2843110332950%29.jpg/250px-20180924-OSEC-LSC-1160_%2843110332950%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:20180924-OSEC-LSC-1160_(43110332950).jpg)

Flooded farmland in [Duplin County, North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duplin_County,_North_Carolina "Duplin County, North Carolina") in the wake of Florence

The large-scale flooding affected swaths of North Carolina's agricultural industry and proved particularly damaging to livestock. Through September 18, the [North Carolina Department of Agriculture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Carolina_Department_of_Agriculture "North Carolina Department of Agriculture") stated 3.4 million chickens and turkeys and 5,500 hogs died in flooded farms. Dozens of farms remained isolated with animals unable to be fed. Piles of manure stored at these farms were swept into swollen rivers,[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-WTVD_0919-132)[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-133) about a dozen pits holding animal waste were damaged by the flooding and debris.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-134)

In total, more than a hundred and thirty hog waste lagoons were compromised, and thirty-three overflowed to the point of discharging their contents into the [Cape Fear River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Fear_River "Cape Fear River") watershed. Media coverage of the hurricane drew comparisons with Hurricane Floyd; [Smithfield Foods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smithfield_Foods "Smithfield Foods"), which owns many of eastern North Carolina's hog farms, had been criticized at the time for allowing the lagoons to overflow, and had promised improvements to prevent future incidents of pollution.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-BetheaSept2018-135)[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-BufordNov2018-136)

On September 16, approximately 5 million gallons of partially treated wastewater spilled into the Cape Fear River after a treatment plant lost power.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-WTVD_0919-132) An estimated 2,000 yd 3 (1,530 m 3) of coal ash from the closed Sutton Power Station near Wilmington was also swept into the river. Torrential rains from the storm itself, estimated at 30 inches (760 mm), also caused a swamp to spill into the cooling pond.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-137) On September 19, the [H.F. Lee Energy Complex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H.F._Lee_Energy_Complex "H.F. Lee Energy Complex") in [Goldsboro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goldsboro,_North_Carolina "Goldsboro, North Carolina") flooded to the point where their three ponds were completely underwater and began releasing coal ash into the Neuse River.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-138)

#### Domestic and zoo animals

During and after the storm made landfall, local rescuers and nationwide donors and organizations worked to aid the many pets that had been left by their owners, or alongside their owners.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-139)[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-140) Others drove to South and North Carolina in order to evacuate animals and bring them outside of the hurricanes impact zone while shelters in other states accepted animals from the states.[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-141) Many rescuers were looking for local residents in need of assistance or evacuation aid, and discovered some animals in flooding cages, some attempting to seek shelter, and some stranded on porches.[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-142)

Zoo animals such as those from the [Virginia Zoo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Zoological_Park "Virginia Zoological Park") were sheltered within indoor and sheltered portions of their enclosures.[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-143) Other zoos such as the [North Carolina Zoo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Carolina_Zoo "North Carolina Zoo") were lightly impacted by the storm and opened on September 18, and offered free admission for evacuees from September 18 to 21.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-144)

### Evacuees

On September 19, after the rain had stopped, a majority of evacuees were urged by officials to stay away from their homes as the rivers continued to rise; the potential threat of floods remained high, roads remained closed, and thousands lacked power to their homes.[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-145) Many individuals whose homes were ruined due to the hurricane were offered aid through Red Cross shelters, rental assistance from FEMA, or utilizing undamaged rental properties until their homes are livable. FEMA utilized Transitional Sheltering Assistance Programs to pay for hotel stays for individuals while they look for more permanent solutions, the programs had 342 households and a total of 1,044 people as of October 3.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-146)

### Power restoration

In the aftermath of the storm, over 40,000 workers from across the US and Canada went to the Carolinas to help restore power, according to the [Edison Electric Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edison_Electric_Institute "Edison Electric Institute").[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-147)

### Roads

The continued flooding closed many major roads for days after the incident. On September 15, [NCDOT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NCDOT "NCDOT") asked drivers to avoid driving in North Carolina altogether, instructing them to take a detour at [Richmond, Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richmond,_Virginia "Richmond, Virginia") using [Interstate 64](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_64 "Interstate 64") west to [Interstate 81](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_81 "Interstate 81") south into [Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee "Tennessee") to [Interstate 40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_40 "Interstate 40") west to [Interstate 75](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_75 "Interstate 75") south into [Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_(U.S._state) "Georgia (U.S. state)") to [Interstate 16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_16 "Interstate 16") east back to [Interstate 95](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_95 "Interstate 95").[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-148) Parts of I-95 and I-40 in North Carolina reopened ten days later September 23, while hundreds of other roads remained closed.[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-149) Thousands of dead fish had to be cleaned off of [Interstate 40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_40_in_North_Carolina "Interstate 40 in North Carolina") in [Pender County, North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pender_County,_North_Carolina "Pender County, North Carolina"), with other marine life such as a 20-foot-long whale being reported washed onto beaches and residential areas, having to be removed and buried.[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-150)

### Relief efforts

[![Image 19](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a3/PenderCounty_Florence_Damage_3.jpg/250px-PenderCounty_Florence_Damage_3.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:PenderCounty_Florence_Damage_3.jpg)

Clean up and volunteering after the storm in Pender County, NC.

President Donald Trump visited North and South Carolina on September 19, and spoke to emergency workers in an [airplane hangar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hangar "Hangar") at the [Marine Corps Air Station Cherry Point](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marine_Corps_Air_Station_Cherry_Point "Marine Corps Air Station Cherry Point").[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-151) He also promised to provide state officials all support needed for search and rescue operations. Further, he promised to ensure that the states would continue to receive help while they were rebuilding after the storm.[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-152) South Carolina Governor McMaster applied for $1.2 billion in federal funding for recovery, including $165 million under the [National Flood Insurance Program](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Flood_Insurance_Program "National Flood Insurance Program") and $125 million for agriculture.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-NPR_0920-83) On September 23, the [United States Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Congress "United States Congress") began to deliberate a $1.7 billion aid package for the Carolinas.[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-153)

### Investigation

After two patients at a mental hospital died when the van carrying them was swept away by floods, the State Law Enforcement Division and Highway Patrol opened an investigation into the incident, and the deputies involved, who were escorting the women and were rescued from the top of the van, were placed on [administrative leave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Administrative_leave "Administrative leave").[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-:0-125)[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-154) Family members of the deceased met with South Carolina elected officials to discuss the incident and the changes that they wish to see put in place to prevent other deaths.[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-155)

### Connection to climate change

See also: [Tropical cyclones and climate change](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_cyclones_and_climate_change "Tropical cyclones and climate change")

A number of studies assessing the effect of global climate change on the impact of Hurricane Florence were performed. Projections prior to landfall made the case that the hurricane could be up to 50% larger and 50 miles wider given the effects of anthropogenic warming. Analyses after the hurricane indicate that warming led to an increase in total rainfall of around 5% and an increase in diameter of around 1.5 miles.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-FlorenceObserver2020-70) When the [Associated Press](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Associated_Press "Associated Press") reached out to seventeen meteorologists and climate scientists following the hurricane, the majority agreed that human-caused warming worsened the effects of the storm. However, a few remain hesitant to make such statements regarding individual hurricanes.[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-WarmerWorld2018-156)

### Retirement

Due to the damage and loss of life in the Carolinas from the storm, the name _Florence_ was retired from the Atlantic rotating naming lists by the [World Meteorological Organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Meteorological_Organization "World Meteorological Organization") in March 2019, and will never again be used for an Atlantic basin tropical cyclone. It was replaced with _[Francine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane\_Francine "Hurricane Francine")_ for the [2024 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Atlantic_hurricane_season "2024 Atlantic hurricane season").[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-157)[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Florence#cite_note-158)
